exposure: Umbilical artery Doppler parameters (Raised RI, PI, S/D ratio)
Uterine artery Doppler parameters (High RI, notching)

High-risk pregnancy factors (chronic or pregnancy-induced hypertension, eclampsia in previous pregnancy, anemia, diabetes mellitus or gestational diabetes mellitus, elderly gravida (>35 years), grand multipara (>=5))
cohort: The study included 150 high-risk pregnant patients with conditions such as chronic or pregnancy-induced hypertension, anemia, diabetes mellitus, elderly gravida (>35 years), or grand multiparity (>=5).
finding: Abnormal umbilical artery Doppler (raised RI, PI, S/D ratio) predicted IUGR, poor perinatal outcome, and risk of intrauterine foetal death, while high RI and/or notching of the uterine artery Doppler were associated with an increased risk of pre-eclampsia.
gest_age: Doppler measurements were taken between 16-22 weeks gestation.
